The Role We are looking for an Engineering Leader to manage and scale multiple product lines in the Voice, BPO, and Workforce Management space. This is a high-impact leadership role that sits at the intersection of real-time voice systems, operations research, and data-intensive platform engineering. You will report directly to the Head of Engineering and own the engineering organization that builds the infrastructure powering Ema’s Voice AI Employees, Agent QA, auto-learning pipelines, rich analytics, and workforce optimization capabilities — all operating as scalable, multi-tenant systems deployed across global geographies. You will collaborate with Product, ML/AI, and Go-to-Market teams to translate customer needs into production systems that handle high volumes of voice data, deliver real-time insights, and continuously improve through automated learning loops. As the owner of multiple product lines, you will balance roadmap priorities across Voice, BPO operations, and WFM (work force management) — ensuring each product evolves cohesively while meeting distinct customer needs. What You Will Do Scalable Multi-Tenant Systems Architect and build multi-tenant systems that serve enterprise customers across geographies with strict data residency, isolation, and compliance requirements. Design high-throughput ingestion systems capable of processing large volumes of voice data, call metadata, and operational telemetry in near real-time. Make foundational architectural decisions on data stores, stream processing, and storage tiers — balancing query performance, cost, and operational simplicity. Champion SOLID principles, clean architecture, and engineering rigor across all codebases — ensuring systems are testable, extensible, and maintainable at scale. Team Building & Engineering Culture Recruit, hire, and develop senior engineers across a multi-disciplinary function spanning voice engineering, backend systems, data engineering, and applied operations research. Establish engineering standards, code review culture, and a strong bias toward shipping — with equal commitment to system reliability and customer experience. Coach and grow senior/staff engineers into technical leaders; manage engineering managers as the organization scales. Drive cross-functional alignment with Product, ML/AI, and Go-to-Market teams to ensure the platform evolves in lockstep with customer needs and market feedback. Voice Platform & Agent QA Own the end-to-end engineering for Ema’s AgentQA capabilities — real-time voice pipelines, telephony integrations, and voice-to-action workflows. Build and scale the Agent QA platform: automated call scoring, compliance monitoring, sentiment analysis, and coaching feedback loops. Design auto-learning systems that continuously improve voice agents from production interactions — closed-loop feedback, model retraining triggers, and quality regression detection. Deliver rich voice analytics: call volume trends, handle time distributions, first-call resolution metrics, agent performance dashboards, and anomaly detection. Build scalable voice pipeline across geographies – keeping in mind PII, security and compliance requirements. Workforce Management & Operations Research Build WFM capabilities including demand forecasting, shift scheduling, real-time adherence monitoring, and capacity planning — applying operations research techniques to optimize workforce utilization. Design and implement optimization algorithms for headcount modeling, skill-based routing, and workload balancing across multi-site, multi-timezone contact center operations. Partner with ML/AI teams to integrate predictive models for call volume forecasting, attrition risk, and staffing efficiency. What We Look For Required 12+ years of software engineering experience, with 4+ years leading engineering teams of 8+ engineers at high-growth startups or top-tier tech companies. Deep expertise in building real-time, data-intensive systems. Strong foundation in data stores and storage systems: relational databases, time-series stores, columnar analytics engines, and caching layers — with the judgment to choose the right tool for the workload. Experience building quality software using AI-driven tools and workflows. Track record of taking products from 0→1 and iterating rapidly based on customer feedback. Hands-on proficiency with SOLID principles, clean architecture, and design patterns — you write and review production code and lead by example on system design. Experience building scalable multi-tenant SaaS platforms with data isolation, geo-distributed deployments, and compliance requirements (SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA). Track record of building ingestion systems for high volumes of load — event-driven architectures, stream processing (Kafka, Flink, or equivalent), and batch/real-time hybrid pipelines. Strong product sense: ability to deeply understand customer problems in contact center, voice, and workforce domains and translate them into clean technical solutions. Proven ability to hire, develop, and retain high-caliber engineers across multiple disciplines in competitive markets. Good to have Experience in voice/telephony systems: WebRTC, SIP, voice-over-IP infrastructure, or contact center platforms. Background in operations research or optimization: scheduling algorithms, linear/integer programming, constraint satisfaction, or demand forecasting models. Experience building analytics platforms: OLAP systems, real-time dashboards, metric computation engines, or BI infrastructure. Prior work on auto-learning or continuous improvement systems: feedback loops from production data, automated retraining pipelines, or quality monitoring systems. Experience with AI/ML-powered products in enterprise settings — agentic automation, LLM orchestration, or AI-driven UX. Familiarity with WFM or contact center operations — staffing models, Erlang-based capacity planning, or real-time adherence systems. Why Ema Build at the intersection of Voice AI, operations research, and enterprise-scale systems — a rare combination of deeply technical challenges with direct customer impact. Shape the engineering foundation of a category-defining AI platform — your architectural decisions will power how the world’s largest enterprises run their voice and workforce operations. data.title: Payment Operations Lead
data.description: Payment Operations Lead Global expansion is broken. Without a local company, conversion rates fall, costs rise, and compliance gets messy. Outpost fixes it. Selling internationally is a maze of tax, payments, and operational friction. Most brands avoid it, or expand slowly and expensively. Outpost is your modular back office for global commerce. Pick only what you need - tax, payments, treasury, or operations - and unlock new markets without the overhead. Sometimes we become liable for a merchant's taxes. Sometimes we become the legal reseller in each market and carry the payments, tax and compliance risk. Other times, we give you the tools to do it yourself. We go live wherever a merchant needs to sell next, for digital and physical goods. That means we own the full stack - payments, tax, compliance, treasury, and merchant experience. Sell anything, anywhere. Without compromise. 🧠 The Role We're looking for a Payment Operations hire to own the part of Outpost where the money actually moves. When we become the legal reseller in a market, we take the payment. Every merchant we onboard gets its own merchant ID and its own merchant category code, never pooled into one shared code, which is exactly why our approval rates beat the alternatives. Keeping that true across every market, every processor and every merchant is the job. This is a quantitative role in an operational seat . You'll live in the transaction data: why authorisation rates differ by market, issuer, card type and hour of day, what a routing change is actually worth, where a 40 basis point cost difference is hiding, which decline codes are recoverable and which are noise. Then you'll act on it, with processors, with engineering, and with merchants. You won't be siloed. Payments at Outpost touches pricing, treasury, tax and the product roadmap, and you'll be pulled into all of it. But your edge is the numbers, and we want someone whose first instinct on any problem is to pull the data and model it. You'll work directly with the founding team and with engineering, who will build what you spec. 🧗 What You'll Get Yes, the work is intense . But in return you'll get scope and exposure most people wait 10 to 20 years to access . You'll own economics that decide whether the company is profitable, negotiate with processors and banks as a principal rather than a customer, and get to see the full machinery of cross-border payments from the inside. We won't handhold, but we'll coach you hard. 🧩 What You'll Do Build the system Run payment operations agentically. Build agentic system that monitor approval rates, triage declines, assemble dispute evidence, chase reconciliation breaks and draft the processor follow-up, so humans only touch the exceptions. You'll design the workflows, set the guardrails, and audit what the agents produce Write the playbooks: new processor onboarding, new market launch, incident response, dispute handling Onboard new processors, banking partners and local acquiring as we launch new markets Own payments performance Own approval rates by market, processor, issuer, card type and merchant, and know why each one moves Build and run routing logic. Decide what goes where, prove the uplift, and iterate Run decline recovery: retry logic, network tokens, account updater, 3DS strategy and exemption handling Run chargeback operations and fraud strategy. Set thresholds, represent disputes, keep merchants inside scheme limits Own the payment incident path. When authorisations drop in one market at, you're the one who spots it and fixes it Own the economics Build full visibility into cost per transaction: scheme fees, interchange, processor margin, FX, and where each one leaks Own processor relationships day to day. Performance reviews, pricing negotiations, new partner evaluation Model the trade-off between approval rate and cost by market, and make the call Feed real payment economics into how we price merchants Own the money movement Settlement, reconciliation and payouts. Every penny accounted for, every break chased down Reserve logic and settlement timing by merchant segment and risk profile Work with treasury on funding, FX exposure and cash timing across our local companies 💥 Example Projects Take a market from a 66% approval rate to 90% or better, and prove exactly which changes did it Build the routing framework that optimises approval rate against cost, market by market Renegotiate processor pricing using our own volume and performance data Build the cost-per-transaction model across every processor and market, and find the basis points nobody is watching Debug delays in settlement and fix them across engineering, operations and the processor Design reserve and settlement logic for a new merchant segment and implement it Cut chargeback rate through better fraud tooling and merchant policy Evaluate and onboard a new processor for local acquiring in Latin America or Asia Build the payments monitoring layer so anomalies find us, not the other way round 🧱 What We're Looking For Ideal background: A STEM or quantitative degree is strongly preferred - mathematics, physics, engineering, computer science, statistics, econometrics or similar. 3 to 7+ years in payment operations, payment analytics, or a data or analytics role that moved into payments, at a processor, acquirer, or high-volume fintech (Adyen, Stripe, Checkout.com , Nuvei, Worldpay, Revolut, Wise, Dojo, Airwallex or similar) Strong analytical skills — advanced Excel or Sheets, experience with BI tools, and the ability to build models and run analyses independently without waiting for a data team. Bonus: experience at platforms that act as the legal reseller (Global-e, Digital River, Paddle), local acquiring outside Europe and the US, interchange and scheme fee economics, or a background in data science or quantitative consulting before payments Signals we care about: Ridiculous bias for action . You solve, you don't observe Analytically strong and commercially sharp. You quantify the opportunity before you argue for it Systems thinker who still does the work. You fix the transaction, then remove the reason it broke Strong EQ. Processors, banks and merchants all need managing, often at the same time Exceptionally hard working . You see work as a core part of your purpose Fluent in ambiguity and chaos. Startups are not neat, this will be hard Curious and resourceful. You can figure anything out Clear, quantified achievements on your CV, not vague descriptions What this role is not: Not a payments strategy role without operational depth. You'll be in the dashboards daily Not a pure analytics role. The analysis is the start, the change is the job Not a narrow specialist seat. Payments here touches pricing, treasury, tax and product Not for someone who needs defined processes and hierarchy to be effective 🚀 Why This Role Is Different Most companies treat payments as a cost centre someone else manages. Here it is the product and the margin at the same time. We take legal responsibility for our merchants' payments. That means a point of approval rate is real revenue for them and real evidence for us, and a basis point of cost is real profit. Very few people get to own that surface this early, with this much data and this little bureaucracy in the way. We expect whoever is in this role to grow rapidly, and we'll back you every step of the way. 🦾 Outpost Team Our team were leaders at Revolut, Airwallex, Adyen and Wayflyer, and we're backed by top-tier investors who have built or backed some of the world's leading fintechs. 🧾 What We Offer Equity and salary in a well-funded startup Ability to own your work and move fast World-class training from operators who've scaled globally A global mission with real impact Low politics, high output Chance to grow into a senior leadership role A culture of builders, not talkers 🧭 Working Style We work together in person in London 5 days a week. data.title: Head of Operations
data.description: 🌍 About Outpost Global expansion is broken. Without a local entity, conversion rates fall, costs rise, and compliance gets messy. Outpost fixes it. Selling internationally is a maze of tax, payments, and operational friction. Most brands avoid it or expand slowly and expensively. Outpost is your modular back office for global commerce. Pick only what you need — tax, payments, treasury, or operations — and unlock new markets without the overhead. Sometimes we act as Merchant of Record, taking on tax and compliance risk. Other times, we give you the tools to do it yourself. We operate across 58+ tax jurisdictions for digital and physical goods. That means we own the full stack — payments, tax, compliance, treasury, and merchant experience. Sell anything, anywhere. Without compromise. 🧠 The Role We're looking for our Head of Operations: the person who owns how Outpost actually runs. Today, operations at Outpost is a set of processes held together by a small group of very good people. Merchant onboarding, KYC/KYB, market launches, tax registrations, payouts, treasury approvals, chargebacks, merchant support — it all works, but it works because people push it. Your job is to turn that into a machine. This is a hands-on leadership role, not a management layer. You'll own the operational stack end to end: onboarding and activation, merchant operations, payments and treasury ops, compliance monitoring, and new market launches. You'll design the processes, build the tooling requirements with engineering, write the playbooks, and then run them yourself until they're good enough to hand over. You'll hire and grow a small team behind you, but for the first stretch you are the team. If your instinct when something breaks is to open the dashboard and fix it rather than schedule a meeting about it, you'll do well here. You'll work directly with the CEO and founding team, and you'll have a real say in what Outpost builds — operations is the sharpest source of product signal we have. 🧗 What You'll Get Yes, the work is intense. But in return, you'll get scope and exposure most people wait 10–20 years to access. You'll own a core function of a company solving one of the hardest problems in global commerce, work with senior stakeholders across PSPs, banks, tax authorities and merchants, and build a team from scratch. We won't handhold, but we'll coach you hard. 🧩 What You'll Do Own the operational stack Own merchant onboarding end to end: applications, KYC/KYB, risk review, activation, time-to-live Run merchant operations day to day — support escalations, payouts, settlements, disputes Own treasury operations: proceeds requests, money movement, reserves, reconciliation Monitor merchant risk and compliance thresholds (chargebacks, fraud, refunds) and act before they become losses Own payment operations alongside engineering: auth rates, routing, decline recovery, chargeback and fraud strategy Build the system, not just the output Turn manual processes into documented, repeatable, measurable playbooks Define the operational metrics that matter and build the reporting so the company can see them Work acquiring in new geographies Build the operational side of new products and merchant segments before they go live Feed market and merchant reality back into the product roadmap Lead Hire, onboard, and grow a small operations team Set standards: what good looks like, how fast we respond, what we never get wrong Be the operational voice in company planning — what we can support, when, and at what cost 💥 Example Projects Redesign merchant onboarding to cut time-to-live by 50% without weakening KYB Build the operational launch playbook for three new markets and run the first one yourself Debug delays in payouts and fix them across engineering, ops, compliance, and PSPs Design reserve and settlement logic for a new merchant segment and implement it Build the ops metrics dashboard: onboarding funnel, time-to-live, ticket volume, payout SLA, chargeback rate Cut chargeback rate through better fraud tooling and merchant policy Spec the next version of our internal ops tooling with engineering and ship it Write the merchant VAT compliance playbook across EU markets with the tax team Hire and onboard the first two operations analysts and get them productive in 30 days 🧱 What We're Looking For Ideal background: 6–10 years in operations at high-growth fintech, payments, or e-commerce infrastructure (Revolut, Stripe, Adyen, Wise, Mollie, Airwallex, Checkout.com , or similar) Has owned a function or a large slice of one — onboarding, merchant ops, payment ops, or risk ops — not just executed within it Experience building processes from zero, not inheriting them Bonus: MoR platforms (Global-e, Digital River, Paddle), cross-border tax exposure, or PSP/acquirer operations Comfortable with data — SQL, spreadsheets, dashboards. data.title: Engineering Summer Internship 2027
data.description: 📍 London 2 days per week with 3 days working remotely 📅 8 week placement - July to August 2027 Our mission Two in five people in the UK rent their homes. Our mission? To provide them with the best renting experience in the world 🌎 We started Goodlord because we wanted to make renting simple and transparent for everyone involved: the agent, the landlord, and the tenant. We knew Generation Rent would lead to more tenants, with higher digital expectations and we were confident we could provide a solution 🏠 Like all scale-ups it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster journey, but we’re now stronger than ever, with around 3,000 letting agents using the platform, exciting and varied products and 350+ Goodlordians across the group supporting the mission! 💚 The Opportunity Develop your programming knowledge further by solving real-world problems using PHP, Python, C# and/or Typescript Deliver features that will affect 1 out of 4 tenants and thousands of estate agents in the UK Experience first-hand what the engineering process is like in a growing business Be mentored by top-class engineers on the first steps in your career. Get paid up to £40,000 (pro-rated) What we need from you Be in the penultimate year of a computer science or related degree Be comfortable coding in a language of your choice and open to learning new ones Be keen to see your work have a real world impact. What’s next? If you’re ready to apply what you’ve been learning to the rental experience while taking your skills to the next level then click apply (2-3 minutes)! A full job spec is available on request Why you'll love being a Goodlordian Aside from the role, the people, our culture and our mission, we have some other things that make Goodlord a pretty awesome place to be. Here’s a few favourites amongst Goodlordians (check out our careers page for more info). Grow with Goodlord: your development is important to us, that’s why we are Great Place to Work - certified . data.title: Risk Operations Analyst
data.description: About Ryft Ryft is a regulated payment facilitator and authorised payment institution building the infrastructure layer for modern commerce platforms. We enable marketplaces, SaaS platforms and multi-party ecosystems to embed and monetise payments natively. Our technology handles onboarding, compliance, orchestration, split payments and revenue sharing, allowing our partners to focus on growth while we manage complexity. We are now entering the next phase of scale, expanding into new verticals and building a category-defining embedded payments platform. About the Role We’re hiring a Risk Operations Analyst to sit within our first line fraud and risk function, reporting to the Fraud & Risk Manager. This role is the operational backbone of how Ryft manages its relationships with acquiring and banking partners, taking inbound queries from our acquires and bank partners and owning them through to resolution. The core of this role is investigative. When a query comes in from a banking partner, we need someone who can trace a transaction end-to-end through our systems, understand what the bank is actually asking, produce a response that meets their expectations, and critically, question what they find along the way rather than closing the thread at the first plausible answer. Alongside partner queries, you’ll carry out merchant risk monitoring as part of the broader fraud and risk operation; reviewing merchant behaviour, flagging anomalies, and feeding intelligence into the fraud detection and response process led by the Fraud & Risk Manager. If you’re someone who digs until they have the full picture, is comfortable navigating between internal systems and external expectations, and takes pride in the quality of what they send to a bank, this role is for you. What You’ll Do Acquirer & Banking Partner Query Management • Act as the primary point of contact for inbound risk and compliance queries from Ryft’s acquiring and banking partners — managing each query through to full resolution. • Trace transactions end-to-end through Ryft’s systems in response to partner queries — reconstructing the payment journey, identifying where issues occurred, and producing clear, accurate responses that meet the bank’s expectations. • Understand what each banking partner needs to see in a response and tailor your output accordingly — whether that’s a transaction trail, a merchant explanation, supporting documentation, or a combination. • Question what you find — don’t close a query at the first plausible answer. If something looks unusual or doesn’t add up, dig further and escalate to the Fraud & Risk Manager where needed. • Maintain a clear log of all partner queries, response timelines, and outcomes, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks and that patterns across queries are surfaced proactively. • Build a working knowledge of each partner’s reporting expectations, query formats, and escalation preferences, reducing friction in ongoing communications. Merchant Risk Monitoring • Carry out day-to-day merchant risk monitoring across the Ryft portfolio — reviewing transaction activity, volumes, and behavioural patterns to identify anomalies that may indicate fraud, policy breach, or elevated risk. • Feed merchant risk intelligence into the fraud detection and response process, working closely with the Fraud & Risk Manager to ensure monitoring activity informs rule tuning and threshold decisions. • Flag merchants or sub-merchants exhibiting patterns of concern, documenting your findings clearly and escalating where a risk response is required. • Support chargeback and dispute monitoring at the merchant level, identifying accounts with elevated dispute rates and feeding that data into the wider fraud analysis process. • Maintain accurate, audit-ready records of monitoring activity and risk decisions in line with FCA expectations and internal policy. Cross-functional Collaboration • Work closely with the Fraud & Risk Manager to ensure partner query intelligence and merchant monitoring findings are connected — a query from an acquirer about a specific merchant should inform, and be informed by, what you’re seeing in monitoring. • Liaise with the underwriting team where partner queries or merchant monitoring activity raises questions about how a merchant was onboarded or what their risk profile should be. • Support the engineering and product teams with information requests related to transaction tracing, where system-level investigation requires cross-functional input. • Contribute to the continuous improvement of response templates, internal runbooks, and query management procedures. What We’re Looking For Essential • Experience in a payments operations, risk operations, or financial crime role within a PSP, acquirer, payment facilitator, or bank — with direct exposure to acquirer or banking partner queries. • Demonstrable ability to trace transactions through payment systems — you understand how a payment moves, where it can go wrong, and how to reconstruct what happened from system data. • Strong written communication skills, with experience producing clear, structured responses to banking or regulatory counterparties who expect precision. • An investigative mindset — you ask the next question, not just the obvious one. You’re not satisfied with a plausible explanation if the evidence doesn’t fully support it. • Organised and reliable under query volume — able to manage multiple open cases simultaneously without losing track of timelines or detail. • Comfortable operating within a first line risk function with real accountability for the quality and timeliness of outputs. Nice to Have • Familiarity with merchant risk monitoring in a PayFac or marketplace payments model. • Experience with chargeback and dispute management, including TC40/SAFE data or scheme fraud reporting. • Exposure to fraud tooling such as Fraud.net , Sift, SEON or equivalent platforms. • SQL or data querying skills for self-serve transaction investigation. data.description: An exciting opportunity to join Leafio as a Quality Officer and play an important role in shaping the future of our pharmaceutical wholesale operations. This is an opportunity to be part of a business at a pivotal stage of its journey, helping to establish and develop our quality processes as we build a compliant, efficient and reliable pharmaceutical supply chain. We are looking for someone who brings hands-on experience within a regulated pharmaceutical environment, a strong understanding of Good Distribution Practice (GDP) and the confidence to take ownership of quality activities in a fast-paced, evolving business. If you enjoy working collaboratively, have a keen eye for detail and want to make a meaningful contribution to a growing organisation, this could be a fantastic next step in your career. What is the job? We are looking for an experienced Quality Officer to join Leafio at a pivotal stage of our growth. This is a unique opportunity to join an ambitious team as we establish our pharmaceutical wholesale operation and secure the licences required to import, store and distribute medicinal products across the UK. As part of the Quality team, you will ensure the daily activities are actioned and monitored and meet the highest standards of Good Distribution Practice (GDP), regulatory compliance and product quality. You will play a critical role in ensuring that all medicinal products received, stored and supplied by Leafio comply with GDP, MHRA requirements (esp Reg 167), internal Quality Management Systems (QMS) standards, and customer expectations. What will you be doing? Ensure that Deviations, change controls, risk management and CAPAs are actioned according to their target date of completion Raise Deviations, change controls, risk managements and CAPAs when needed and support in the investigations where relevant Maintain and update the QMS (SOPs, policies, forms, logs) Draft standard operating procedures, distribute for reviewing and finalising the procedures Manage document control, versioning, training records and archiving Support preparation of quality management review Deliver GDP and QMS training to the relevant departments where needed Support with batch traceability, Certificate of Analysis (CoA) documentation and batch release confirmations/verifications Support with customers’ complaints and ensure timelines are adhered to Support the Responsible Person (RP) in maintaining compliance and safeguarding product quality throughout the supply chain. Actively collaborating with cross-functional teams (e.g. pharmacy, warehouse) Participating and supporting in audits (internal/external) and inspections where required Any other tasks deemed necessary by the Responsible Person (RP) What do you need? Knowledge of Good Manufacturing (GMP) or Good Distribution Practice (GDP) and the regulatory framework governing pharmaceutical wholesale and distribution Proven experience working within a GMDP regulated pharmaceutical environment, (ideally supporting wholesale distribution and importation), with more than 2 years experience Proven experience of dealing with a Quality Management Systems (QMS), including but not limited to Complaints, CAPAs, Deviations risk management, change control, self inspections/internal audits Proven experience in dealing with unlicensed products (especially in accordance with Regulation 167) Excellent attention to detail and analytical skills Strong communication and report-writing ability Highly organised, able to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines Desirable Experience or exposure to Importation of unlicensed products from outside the EEA Experience in working with an ERP system Previous experience working within the medical cannabis sector Previous experience in releasing products (QC-Quality control) What we offer: Generous Leave: 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year three + 8 bank holidays Pension Matching: Up to 5% employer matching contributions Private Healthcare Scheme Flexibility and Wellness: Work-from-home options, cycle-to-work scheme, and more Growth Opportunities: Collaborate across teams and represent Montu at events, with support to grow your skills and impact Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave About Us At Leafio, we’re building a smarter, more resilient pharmaceutical supply chain that gives pharmacies fast and reliable access to the medicines they need, when they need them. By working directly with manufacturers and creating a more efficient wholesale model, we’re improving stock availability, simplifying distribution and helping to make medicines more affordable for patients. Everything we do is focused on creating a supply chain that is responsive, transparent and equipped to better support healthcare providers across the UK. We are an ambitious, fast-growing business with exciting plans for the future. This is an opportunity to make a genuine impact, help shape how we grow and join a team that is modernising pharmaceutical distribution from the ground up. data.title: Clinical Pharmacist
data.description: At Montu, we are transforming access to medical cannabis treatment across the UK, and our Clinical Pharmacists play an important role in delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care. We are looking for an experienced Clinical Pharmacist (Independent Prescriber) to join our growing London team. This is an opportunity to use your clinical expertise in an evolving area of healthcare, working alongside a multidisciplinary team to support patients throughout their treatment journey. Whether you already have experience in cannabis-based medicinal products or are looking to develop your knowledge in this specialist field, we offer the training and support to help you build your expertise while making a meaningful difference to patients' lives. What is the job? As a Clinical Pharmacist (Independent Prescriber), you will provide safe, effective and personalised treatment to patients with a wide range of clinical needs. Working closely with our multidisciplinary team, you will be responsible for clinically reviewing prescriptions, prescribing appropriate treatments and providing expert clinical guidance to patients and colleagues. You will also contribute to the development of clinical pathways, support patient and staff education and play an important role in maintaining the highest standards of clinical care. This is a hybrid position based at our King's Cross office in London, requiring three days on site and two days working remotely. Please note you will be required to work 1 Saturday per month onsite, for which a day in lieu will be given. What will you be doing? Clinically check and review cannabis-based medicinal product (CBPM) prescriptions to ensure safety, accuracy and appropriateness. Prescribe medicines as an Independent Prescriber, tailoring treatment to individual patient needs. Provide expert clinical guidance to patients and prescribers on treatment options. Maintain accurate and comprehensive patient records in accordance with GPhC standards. Support the dispensary team with complex clinical queries and prescribing-related matters. Deliver education and training on CBPM to patients, clinicians and colleagues. Collaborate with the wider Clinical and Pharmacy teams to ensure a safe and effective patient journey. Contribute to the development of clinical pathways and improvements in patient care. Ensure all clinical activities are conducted in accordance with professional, regulatory and organisational standards. What are we looking for? GPhC registered pharmacist with an Independent Prescriber (IP) qualification. A minimum of two years of prescribing experience. Experience working within a clinical setting. Previous knowledge or experience of cannabis-based medicinal products is desirable but not essential, as specialist training will be provided. Excellent communication skills, with the confidence to engage with patients and clinical colleagues. Strong clinical judgement and the ability to make safe, evidence-based prescribing decisions. Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities. A proactive, resourceful and solutions-focused approach. High attention to detail and a commitment to patient safety and clinical governance. A collaborative approach and the ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team. What do we offer? Generous Annual Leave: 25 days holiday, increasing to 27 days after one year and 30 days after three years, plus 8 bank holidays. Pension Contributions: Employer pension matching of up to 5%. Private Healthcare Scheme. Hybrid Working: A combination of office-based and remote working. Cycle-to-Work Scheme: Supporting healthier and more sustainable commuting. data.title: Medical Lead
data.description: Are you an experienced doctor with a passion for developing others and delivering exceptional patient care? At Montu, we are looking for a Medical Team Lead to join our growing Clinical team, combining clinical practice with the opportunity to lead, mentor and develop a team of doctors. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys supporting others, has experience providing clinical guidance and supervision, and is confident in building strong working relationships with clinicians and consultants. You will play a key role in supporting the professional development of our Junior Clinical Fellows (JCFs), helping them build confidence, develop greater clinical autonomy and deliver safe, high-quality patient care. As we continue to grow, this is an opportunity to bring your clinical expertise and leadership skills into an evolving area of healthcare, helping to shape and support the next generation of clinicians while making a meaningful difference to patients' lives. What is the job? As a Medical Team Lead, you will provide day-to-day leadership, support and guidance to a team of clinicians, ensuring they are well-supervised, well-supported, and progressing safely towards greater clinical autonomy. You will act as the primary link between clinicians and consultants, coordinating supervision, escalation pathways, and feedback loops so that patient care stays safe and consistent. You will combine your own clinical practice with people leadership, taking ownership of fellow development, consultant engagement, governance, and training within your team, while working alongside other Team Leads to keep standards consistent across the wider service. You will be the first point of contact for JCF’s requiring guidance on professional or personal development and appraisal or revalidation. You will also act as a trusted contact for consultants raising concerns about supervision and workload. What will you be doing? Clinician Line Management Act as the named line manager/lead for a cohort of clinicians, providing day-to-day leadership, coaching, and pastoral support. Conduct regular 1:1s with each fellow, tracking progress against objectives, competencies, and rotation/training milestones. Identify clinicians who are struggling early, and put support plans in place in collaboration with consultants and HR/medical education leads. Assist with the onboarding and induction experience for new clinicians — inductions, shadowing, buddy systems, and early check-ins. Support the management of day-to-day workforce logistics for the clinicians: rota input, leave requests, sickness/absence, and shift coverage, working with the operations team. Recognise and celebrate good performance, and manage underperformance or conduct concerns through appropriate, documented processes alongside our HR team. Consultant Engagement Build and maintain strong working relationships with consultants. Act as the escalation point for consultants — surfacing concerns about supervision quality, caseload, or clinical support gaps. Coordinate consultant and JCF annual appraisals or revalidation. Gather and act on consultant feedback regarding clinical safety and any recurring themes. Support scheduling and coverage conversations with consultants (clinics, on-call, teaching sessions). Clinical & Patient Support Act as a point of escalation for complex clinical cases and patient concerns. Support clinicians through complaints, incidents, and governance issues involving their clinical decisions. Provide direct clinical mentoring, and know when to route a case to a consultant. Promote safe prescribing and adherence to clinical standards appropriate to clinicians’ training level. Governance, Quality & Audit Support compliance with clinical policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements across the fellow cohort. Support clinical audits and quality improvement projects, involving clinicians in QI work as a development opportunity. Analyse audit and incident themes specific to JCFs (e.g. common escalation triggers, training gaps) and use these to shape training priorities. Work with governance and operational teams on regulatory readiness. Operational Excellence & Change Monitor clinician workload, rota adherence, professionalism and service coverage; flag risks early. Contribute to process improvements that affect how fellows are supervised, escalate, or are trained. Track and report on team performance metrics: fellow progression, incident trends, audit outcomes, consultant feedback themes. Collaborate with other Team Leads to keep clinician management and consultant engagement approaches consistent across services. Training & Education Support the induction programmes for incoming clinicians from a medical perspective. Identify individual and cohort-wide development needs, working with consultants and training and education teams to close gaps. Involvement in the organisation and/or deliver teaching sessions and case reviews. Champion a culture of learning, feedback, and continuous improvement across the fellow-consultant relationship. This list is not exhaustive. As the business evolves, responsibilities may change and develop over time. What do you need? GMC registration with an active licence to practise and good professional standing. Experience supervising, managing, or mentoring junior doctors/clinical fellows is desirable. Experience working alongside or liaising with consultants in a clinical or operational capacity is desirable. Understanding of clinical governance, incident management, complaints handling, audit, and quality improvement. Confidence managing sensitive people-management conversations (performance, wellbeing, escalations). Strong communication skills, with the ability to influence both junior and senior clinicians. Experience working within digital healthcare, telemedicine, private healthcare, or fast-paced healthcare environments is desirable. Comfortable using clinical systems, rostering tools, and healthcare technology platforms. Adaptable, proactive, and solutions-focused, with a genuine interest in developing junior talent. What we offer: Generous Leave : 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year three + 8 bank holidays Pension Matching : Up to 5% employer matching contributions Private Healthcare Scheme Flexibility and Wellness : Work-from-home options, cycle-to-work scheme, and more Growth Opportunities : Collaborate across teams and represent Montu at events, with support to grow your skills and impact Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave About Us Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis-based medicines (CBPM), dedicated to improving patient access to safe and effective treatments. Our mission is to transform lives by combining innovative technology with high-quality clinical care, ensuring patients receive the support they need at every step of their journey. As a fast-growing organisation, we offer a collaborative and supportive environment where talented people can develop their careers while contributing to meaningful change in healthcare. At Montu UK, your work has a direct impact on improving patients’ lives and expanding access to modern medical treatments. Compensation: £70K • £70K Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

data.title: Consultant Psychiatrist PAYE
data.description: An opportunity to help patients who have run out of options For many people living with chronic pain, the journey has been long. They have tried multiple medications, procedures and therapies, yet their pain continues to impact every aspect of daily life. By the time they reach us, many are looking for another option where conventional treatment has fallen short. We are Montu UK, one of the UK's largest medical cannabis clinics, and we are looking for Consultants specialising in Pain Management to join our clinical team. About the role You will assess and manage patients exploring cannabis based medicines, making the clinical decision on whether treatment is appropriate and managing their care from there. This is an evolving area of medicine where the evidence base continues to grow, giving you the opportunity to help shape how cannabis based medicines are used within pain management in the UK. You do not need previous experience with cannabis based medicines. We are looking for experienced Pain Management Consultants with sound clinical judgement, an open mind and a genuine interest in improving outcomes for patients with complex chronic pain. We provide comprehensive specialist training, and our multidisciplinary model means you are never working in isolation. Nurses and pharmacists complete pre consultation and follow up prescribing tasks, allowing you to focus on clinical decision making and patient care. What you will be doing: Provide high quality care for patients seeking medical cannabis treatment. Conduct patient consultations, including assessment and ongoing management. Engage in clinical outcome data collection to support evidence based practices. Contribute to clinical governance and maintain robust patient care standards. Collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary team, including nurses and pharmacists. Participate in ongoing training and professional development, including bespoke specialist training in cannabis based medicines (CBMPs). What you need: Full GMC Registration Completion of Specialist Training (CCST/CCT) or equivalent certification On the GMC Specialist Register for Pain Demonstrated interest in alternative therapies Willingness to participate in data collection and reporting Why join us? Highly Competitive Salary: £190,000 - £275,000 FTE, pro rata for part time roles based on experience and hours worked. Flexible Working: Full time or part time options available Comprehensive Indemnity Coverage: Montu will cover all professional and clinical indemnity insurance for your work with us Private Healthcare Work-Life Balance: No night shifts or on call requirements Cutting Edge Training: Access to CPD accredited medical cannabis education and specialist in house training from industry leaders Collaborative Environment: Join a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals Personal Growth: Be part of a pioneering field and shape the future of medical cannabis care in the UK Training & Development: Attendance at a recognised Medical Cannabis Course for Specialist Physicians (sponsored by Montu) Specialist training delivered by experts, including Prof Anup Mathew (Consultant Psychiatrist) and Dr Gerard Sinovich (Pain Management Consultant). Ongoing support and training on clinical protocols, prescribing practices, and Montu’s system usage Working arrangements: Remote Role: Flexible working hours and days Session Structure: Standard session length: 4 hours Appointment duration: 15 minutes (new and existing patients) Montu’s multidisciplinary model allows consultants to focus on prescribing and patient care, while nurses and pharmacists handle pre consultation and follow up tasks. If you are passionate about innovative patient care, thrive in a dynamic environment, and are looking to make a real impact in the field of medical cannabis, we would love to hear from you! Sessions: Each standard session consists of 4 hours of patient consultations. Clinicians can choose their preferred working days and hours, with sessions spread flexibly if needed. To support onboarding, clinicians are required to commit to a minimum of 2 sessions per week/ 8 hours initially, to ensure they become proficient with Montu’s platform. Appointment Durations: Appointments are 15 minutes in length for new and existing patients as Montu operates a multidisciplinary approach, leveraging a clinical skills mix where nurses and pharmacists handle pre-consultation and follow-up prescribing tasks allowing Consultants to focus on prescribing and patient care. About MONTU Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis based medicines (CBPM). We are committed to transforming lives by improving access to safe, effective treatments and offering an exceptional standard of care. Our dynamic and supportive work environment is the perfect place for you to grow professionally while making a meaningful impact on patients’ lives. data.title: Senior Solutions Architect (OEM)
data.description: About Aiven Aiven is the open source based data platform that builders trust to run PostgreSQL®, Apache Kafka®, ClickHouse®, OpenSearch®, Valkey™ and more in production, on any cloud. Builders ship faster. Their companies run on data that stays available, secure + under control. The role You are the technical owner of Aiven's strategic OEM partnerships, from the first pre-sales conversation to production at volume and beyond. OEM partners embed the Aiven platform inside their own products, so their architecture decisions become ours at scale: one design choice gets copied across hundreds of their customers. You win the technical evaluation, run the proof of concept, design the architecture, and stay on as the person both sides trust to say what should be built, what should be automated + what should be cut. You work AI-native. Agents handle deployment analysis, usage monitoring, rightsizing, PoC scaffolding + first-draft documentation; your time goes on the judgment calls, the partner's engineers + the hard integration problems. You own how your work gets done and redesign it as the tools improve, without waiting for a playbook. Life at Aiven Our values shape how we work. Get it done, together: we move with urgency, align on shared outcomes + put our effort where customers feel it most. Invent + impress: we challenge the status quo + bring different perspectives to hard problems. We commit + deliver: we own our commitments + do what we say. In this role, that means working with Sales, Technical Account Managers, Product, Engineering + Support on every partner, being the person partners trust to follow through, and moving faster than the partner's other vendors. We know what needs doing; the risk is being slow. Diverse perspectives make better ideas. Come as you are. We hire for how you think + what you can do. What we offer: stock options, an individual learning budget + coaching, flexible working hours + hybrid working, private health + dental care, and the equipment you need. What you will do Win the technical evaluation Partner with Sales as the technical lead through the OEM sales cycle: discovery, architecture proposals, objection handling + commercial-technical trade-offs. Scope + run proofs of concept that answer the partner's real question, using agents to scaffold environments, generate test data + document results so the PoC takes days, not weeks. Translate complex technical detail into clear business value for non-technical buyers, and the reverse for engineers. Design the architecture Develop and maintain expert-level knowledge of the Aiven platform: every service, feature and limit. Understand each OEM partner's customer use cases, then design and evolve robust, scalable, secure architectures that set them up right from day one, for the workloads they run today and the ones they are building next Guide partners in building architectures that support their customers' use cases, with best practices and tailored recommendations. Work with AI to continuously improve existing processes to build efficiency in the work with partners Enable the partner, from roll-out to growth Get partners up and running: integrate Aiven into their infrastructure + workflows via APIs, SDKs, Terraform + best practices, and solve the problems that block go-live. Actively contribute to partner stability, enablement + growth: help partners consume Aiven services well, so utilisation + value grow together. Work with partners on clear positioning of their Aiven-powered solutions to their customers. Run technical training + workshops for partner teams, including how to build, operate + support the platform with agents in the loop. Keep reference architectures + integration guides current, with agents drafting from real deployments and you owning accuracy. Own the relationship + the resolution Build trust-based relationships with partner engineering teams, technical decision makers + the Aiven sales reps you work alongside. Act as the technical liaison between partners and Product, Engineering + Support. When a partner is blocked, own it end-to-end across teams rather than handing it off. Close the loop fast: partner feedback becomes Product + Engineering tickets the same week, with evidence attached. What you bring 5+ years in solutions architecture, pre-sales, solutions engineering or technical consulting for software or cloud infrastructure, with production experience across data technologies such as Kafka, PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, ClickHouse or similar. Experience with OEM, embedded or ISV partnerships, where your architecture ships inside someone else's product. A record of running proofs of concept that address real business requirements and convert to production. Fluency in at least one programming language, such as Java, Python or Go, and comfort in Linux: installation, securing systems, storage + networking basics like DNS. Working knowledge of at least one public cloud (AWS, Google Cloud or Azure) across compute, storage (block + object), networking + security. Hands-on experience with streaming frameworks (Apache Kafka, Apache Flink, Spark Streaming or Kinesis) and a strong understanding of search ecosystems (OpenSearch, Elasticsearch or Lucene). Daily, hands-on use of AI tools + agents in your technical work, with examples of work you have redesigned or cut as a result. High agency: a record of owning problems end-to-end across teams without waiting for a blueprint. Clear communication with engineers, executives + non-technical buyers, written + spoken, in English, and the ability to build trust quickly with both internal sales reps and external partners. Self Development: In Aiven we’ve a budget to assist continuous learning and the right person will be self motivated to push their boundaries. Nice to have Multi-cloud experience across AWS, Google Cloud + Azure. Terraform, Kubernetes + infrastructure-as-code in production. Familiarity with distributed storage, NoSQL databases + data lakes. Comfort with usage based or consumption pricing, and with using usage data to spot risk + opportunity. Public speaking or technical writing for a developer audience. Contributions to open source projects. How we measure success Partner growth is our top priority Technical win rate on OEM opportunities you lead, and PoC-to-production conversion. Partner time-to-production for new integrations, falling over time. Optimisation recommendations delivered + adopted by partners. Cost or performance issues caught before the partner's customers see them. Partner feedback turned into shipped product changes. Ambassador output: blogs, talks + webinars delivered each year. Reusable assets (agents, reference architectures, playbooks) adopted by the wider SA team. Share of time on partner-facing work vs. analysis + documentation, trending the right way quarter on quarter. Amazing! Choose the equipment you need to set yourself up for success. Use your Professional Development Plan budget for learning opportunities. Receive holistic wellbeing support through our global Employee Assistance Program. data.title: Customer Success Specialist German and English Speaking
data.description: 👋🏻 Hello, we're Laka For this role you will need to speak English and German and have technical bike knowledge! You might not have heard of us yet - that's OK, you've found us now - come and find out more about our journey... Founded in 2017, Laka set out to transform insurance by connecting passionate cyclists to form a collective and protect their bikes for when things go wrong - a better model for insurance was born. For once people come first in insurance by fairly sharing the cost amongst each other. We exist to rewrite the rules of insurance so it’s something people stand with, not against. Our model: Laka makes sure everything runs smoothly for The Collective - from exceptionally fast claims, splitting the cost fairly, guaranteeing a maximum price and all the other heavy lifting of a regulated insurance business. For that service, the collective pays Laka a fee relative to the claims in a month. Take a closer look at exactly what this means and how it works here . What have we been up to since then...? In a nutshell, we've been very busy! Here are a few of the massive achievements we've had: 🚀 Raised an awesome Series B investment round 🚀 Grown the team to over 70 Lakanauts, based across the UK, NL and France, enabling a choice-based, hybrid way of working 🚀 Launched Laka in a total of 11 countries, essentially helping more people in more places! 🚀 Captured the UK, NL and French enthusiast cyclist market and expanded into commercial business partnering 🚀 Been awarded 'Best Cycle Insurance Provider' (for the past 8 years in a row - go us! 🥳) 🚀 Opened 3 shiny new offices in London, Bristol & Amsterdam to provide spaces for people to collaborate as they like 🚀 We've also achieved a 5* rating on Google Reviews and Glassdoor - go check us out! Help us continue to change an outdated industry... We’re growing real fast on our path to make the Laka collective model the industry standard and we’re expanding across segments, products, and territories. We’re looking for innovative, bold and brave minds to help us build the world’s best insurance company. 🤘🏼 The role Customer Experience (CX) at Laka CX are firmly at the heart of why Laka was created - we exist to be there for people when shit happens - our CX function is where this magic takes place... You'll be a key part of our Customer Experience team. Providing a great customer experience is the most important part of our plans to grow the Laka brand internationally. As part of a small, dedicated function (we currently have a team of 11 superstars), you'll be the first point of contact for general and claim-related enquiries. What you'll be getting up to: Supporting Laka customers (& potential customers) with general questions about Laka's products & services, their bicycle insurance and new initiatives via web chat and email Help Laka members to file their claims and guide them through the process of replacing or repairing their bikes and kit either directly with us or by coordinating with third-parties (shops, manufacturers, distributors etc) Be the first point of contact for our B2B partners, supporting them to get their riders back on the road Work closely with the CX team across both the UK and NL to provide a convenient, swift and seamless experience to our members Collate feedback from the collective on an ongoing basis and produce actionable intel to support decision making, both in the CX team and others around Laka Get stuck into our squad-based work, with the goal to continue to make Laka the best it can be (you might find yourself working on exciting projects with the Marketing, Product or Technology teams) Requirements 👉🏻 This role will be a great fit if you: We require that you speak English and German Have a super strong empathy for cyclists and what it means when someone has their bike nicked, damaged or injures themselves whilst out & about on their bike Have a decent understanding of technical terms in cycling (we can bring you up to speed with the latest bike tech), so you can best support all types of customers with whatever query is thrown your way Get loads of satisfaction from helping people going through a rough patch (losing your bike isn't easy, you know) - you'll understand what it means to go the extra mile and make a member's day Enjoy learning new things, working with a lovely bunch of people, and ultimately playing a huge part in the future of Laka! Are a fast learner and can get up to speed with common tools - we use a number of systems at Laka, but don't worry, we'll give you all the training you need Are comfortable chatting with our members, with excellent written communication in (native) German & English You might have already guessed it but it makes a lot of sense to be passionate about cycling when joining Laka. Don't worry about any insurance knowledge - we can teach you the ins-and-outs of insurance and support your knowledge on all things bike parts, too. We can work together on completing your skill set. Benefits 🌟 Our perks What can you expect from working at Laka? 🏠 Remote-first way of working - you choose whether you work from home or our beautiful offices in London & Bristol (we have no minimum expectation of how many days you come in, although we'd love to see your friendly face!) 📈 Share options - we want you to be rewarded for Laka's success - everyone in the business is granted share options when they join 💰 Company bonus scheme - if the company hits its targets, you'll get a cash bonus of 5% of your base salary annually 🌴 Annual leave - 25 days holiday (plus bank holidays), with the option to roll over up to 5 days per year 💶 Pension scheme - Laka pays 3% of your base salary into your pension to help you save for the future 💊 Private medical insurance - we’ll give you individual private cover, with the option to add partners & dependants too (at a small cost) 🍽 Lunch on us - £15 every first Wednesday of the month to enjoy lunch on Laka - pop out locally with people in the office, or order-in at home, the choice is yours 💃 Company-wide events - we love getting everyone together as much as possible - expect regular events throughout the year, for team building, bonding, and general good old-fashioned fun! 🎳 Monthly socials - as if quarterly company events weren't enough, we also give each office a budget for a monthly social activity (think anything from low-key dinner & drinks through to adventure golf, paddleboarding, bowling, electric darts, trampoline parks and more!) 👚 Laka swag - we'll give you some lovely Laka kit to get you started, including a jumper & t-shirts so you can feel (& look) like part of the family 🚴 Laka credit - for all you cyclists, we'll give you £10 credit per month towards insuring your bike(s) with us - plus give you access to a bunch of cycling industry discounts 🧠 Mental health support - unlimited support via Spill, including one-to-one therapy sessions 🌈 Belonging at Laka We're committed to building and sustaining a business that promotes diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging - our customer collective is broad and inclusive, and we'd like our own people to be too. We're fast becoming a global community of people and we believe each person's unique qualities should be celebrated as they are a huge part of what makes Laka a great place to be. We'd love you to bring your authentic self to work every single day, no matter your age, ethnicity, religion, citizenship, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability status, caring responsibilities, neurodiversity, or anything else that makes you, you. data.title: Senior Application Security Engineer
data.description: About Nabla Nabla delivers a unified clinical AI platform used by healthcare organizations across specialties and care settings. The platform includes: Ambient AI documentation that captures clinical conversations and generates structured notes. AI-powered dictation and clinical workflow tools embedded directly within EHR systems. Agentic AI capabilities that support multi-step clinical and administrative tasks. Enterprise-grade infrastructure built for secure deployment across health systems. About the Role We are scaling our healthcare AI platform, with more products, integrations and AI agents, and more protected health information (PHI) flowing through them. To keep pace, we're growing our security engineering team and looking for an exceptional Senior Security Engineer . Our cloud infrastructure handles highly sensitive healthcare data, so security is core to everything we do. Our engineers already ask the right questions every day: can we use a one-time token here? How long should it live? How do we scope this OAuth Client? You'll work directly with our Lead Security Engineer to bring real AppSec expertise into the product squads, and to strengthen security well beyond them. This is a hands-on, high-impact role. About half your time goes to AppSec , but it is deliberately a broad security engineering role, not a pure code-review or pentest job. You'll regularly cross into platform and cloud, CI/CD and detection, and you'll own problems from start to finish. Code scanning, SCA and AI-driven code review are already running, but there is no AppSec process to undo. The threat-modeling practice, the security review loop, the triage rhythm and the secure-by-default libraries don't exist yet. You'll build them and run them. If you're pragmatic, love working shoulder to shoulder with developers, and want your work to protect patients' most sensitive data, this role is for you. Responsibilities Partner with the product squads as their go-to security engineer: design reviews, per-feature threat modeling, and fast, opinionated answers on authN/authZ, tokens and session design. Secure our authentication and authorization surfaces (OAuth clients, one-time codes, multi-org tenancy, the Core API user API, embedded/postMessage SDKs) and hunt for BOLA, IDOR and broken access control before attackers do. Run the code-security findings loop: triage and prioritize results from our SAST, SCA, secrets and IaC scanners and AI-driven code review, route them to the right owners with SLAs, and drive the dependency-vulnerability backlog down, fixing issues yourself when that's faster. Secure our AI/LLM features and internal agents, covering prompt injection, tool and permission scoping for autonomous agents, PHI leakage, de-identification assurance and model/API egress. Run the external testing program: scope and run pentests (web, mobile, backoffice), validate fixes, operate our vulnerability disclosure program, and stand up a bug bounty. Build secure-by-default guardrails (secure coding guidelines, hardened libraries and patterns, pre-commit and PR checks) so the secure path is the easy path. Qualifications 5 to 8+ years in security engineering, including at least 2 to 3 years in application or product security, or experience as a software engineer with a strong security focus. Deep understanding of modern web and API security: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, session and token design, multi-tenancy, and the OWASP Top 10 and API Top 10. You can find access-control flaws by reading code. Strong coder, comfortable reading and fixing production code (mostly Kotlin and Python, plus web, mobile and desktop clients) and automating in Python. Experience running threat modeling and security design reviews, and operating SAST, SCA and secrets scanning in CI with a real triage loop, not just a dashboard. Genuine breadth: comfortable moving between an API design review, a supply-chain hardening PR and an incident in the same week, and honest about what you don't know yet. Excellent communicator who earns developers' trust and works well with engineering, compliance and IT. Full professional fluency in French and English (oral and written). Nice to have: LLM / AI agent security, mobile app security, pentest or bug bounty experience, GCP / GKE, or experience in healthcare or another regulated industry. Life at Nabla When you join Nabla, you join a team that is driven by excellence, curiousity, and kindness. Together, we’re committed to making clinicians’ lives easier and improving healthcare experiences for everyone. We believe clinicians should be able to focus on what they were trained to do, caring for their patients, and that no patient should feel their visit was rushed. We work hard and make time to have fun, too. Our #nablabla channel is just as active as #feature-show-off . We support well-being with workday activities at least three times a week; choose from yoga, running, Pilates, or HIIT. We also host regular off-sites, meet up across New York, Paris, San Francisco, and other cities, and keep the chocolate and nuts well stocked. If this sounds like an environment where you’ll thrive, we look forward to reading your application. Our Values at Nabla Joining Nabla means being part of a team that shares a commitment to excellence, humility, growth, and inclusion. Every day is a new chance to excel We aim for nothing less than the best and are willing to put in the effort and dedication required to exceed standards. We learn from yesterday’s failures and do better every day. Stay humble There’s no place for ego in our team. Our collective success is more important than individual achievements. We see humility as wisdom — keeping focus on the bigger picture. Feedback is a gift We embrace feedback and foster a culture of trust and respect that helps everyone grow. We communicate openly about both achievements and challenges, and we actively involve each other in finding solutions. Committed to diversity We recognize the ongoing challenge of diversity in tech. Our responsibility starts with fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels empowered to be their authentic selves and do their best work. Diversity & Inclusion Diversity and inclusivity are fundamental values at Nabla. We embrace individuals from various backgrounds, including race, gender, educational history, sexual orientation, and beyond. As an equal opportunity employer, we actively seek out and welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds, believing that a wide range of perspectives enriches our team and enhances our ability to innovate and thrive. If you’re contacted by a Nabla recruiter, please ensure they are utilizing a nabla.com email address. We will never ask for the exchange of any money or credit card details during the recruitment process. Nabla utilizes a hiring platform for all applications; please be aware of any suspicious email activity. You can find more information following this link . Requirements Chez Excelya, nous encourageons chacun à faire preuve d'audace et à développer son potentiel. Nous recherchons des professionnels partageant nos valeurs et souhaitant évoluer dans un environnement stimulant. Une connaissance des installations électriques et utilités industrielles constitue un atout. Formation : Diplôme d'Ingénieur généraliste, Génie Industriel, Génie Civil ou équivalent. data.title: Business Development Representative (French)
data.description: 💡 As a Business Development Representative , you will play a key role in Flinn’s go-to-market success by building and qualifying a strong pipeline of high-quality opportunities. You will work at the intersection of Sales, Marketing, and Events , identifying the right prospects, starting meaningful conversations, and setting up the Sales team for successful first meetings. In this role, you will combine structured prospecting with curiosity, persistence, and strong communication skills to engage senior stakeholders at complex B2B organizations. Fluency in French is required (and in Spanish is preferred) , as you will actively engage prospects across these markets. The role is based in Paris, France and includes regular collaboration with the broader go-to-market team as well as travel for conferences and customer meetings . Why Flinn? We are building a truly exceptional culture: While many companies claim to have a great culture, we invite you to discover what truly sets ours apart. Visit our career page , speak with our team, listen to our founders’ podcast, or experience our culture first-hand during the interview process. Make a Meaningful Impact: Your work at Flinn contributes directly to solutions that improve people’s health and lives by making high-quality health products accessible for everyone. Experienced, well-funded, highly professional : As well-funded startup veterans, we know how to sustain long-term business health and success, ensuring an environment for continuous personal growth. What’s in it for you? Join a fast-growing, well-funded European startup backed by experienced founders and investors. Be part of a mission-driven health-tech company whose work directly improves people’s lives. Play a key role in scaling Flinn’s GTM , shaping how we grow. Work in a high-trust, low-ego environment with autonomy and clear ownership. Work in a net-zero company where all unavoidable CO₂ emissions are compensated with carefully selected, high-quality removal certificates. Receive one of the most employee-friendly equity packages , including fair vesting terms and profit-sharing opportunities. Grow in a professional, high-standard environment that supports long-term personal and career development. Your contributions to our journey: Contribute to a strong prospecting strategy: identify and prioritize high-potential businesses across your region that are an ideal fit for Flinn. Build a healthy pipeline: generate new opportunities through targeted outreach, discovery, and account research. Qualify and book introductory meetings: set high-quality first conversations for the Sales team with the right stakeholders. Nurture early-stage opportunities: maintain momentum with emerging leads to develop future pipeline. Collaborate with Marketing & Events: convert conferences, webinars, and field activities into qualified opportunities and measurable pipeline. What you need to be successful: Strong communication, storytelling, and relationship-building skills with the ability to engage diverse stakeholders. Highly energetic: being a self-starter is an absolute must. Fluent in French, and English (written and spoken); fluency Spanish is a plus. Persistent and driven: you thrive on overcoming objections and turning them into positive outcomes Adaptability is key: you’re constantly trying new approaches, new tools, see what works, and what doesn’t Willingness to travel for business meetings, conferences, and company events. Attributes we are looking for: 1+ year of experience in a commercial role, ideally as a BDR (or adjacent). Proven experience running outbound sales motions (prospecting, outreach, qualification, and meeting-setting). Entrepreneurial mindset and/or experience —comfortable taking ownership and operating in ambiguity. Detail-oriented and highly organized, with strong problem-solving skills and excellent follow-through. Committed to high-quality execution and consistently meeting deadlines. 🇪🇺 At this stage of our company, we can only accept applications from people who are based in Europe with either European citizenship, an active working visa or being self-employed and joining us as a full-time contractor (Except for US-based roles). data.title: Research Engineer, GPU Performance
data.description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. About the Role As a Research Engineer, GPU performance , you will sit at the heart of that spectrum: your low-level work directly determines how fast our frontier models can be trained and served. Working hand-in-hand with Research Scientists, you'll make every GPU count. Mistral AI is hiring an expert in pushing large language model's GPU utilization and performance to their limits.. In this role, you will own the performance of our models end-to-end: writing the low-level code that extracts the maximum capacity from high-end hardware, and rethinking model architectures so they run efficiently at scale. What You Will Do Develop low-level code that takes full advantage of high-end GPUs and maxes out their capacity — from custom kernels to memory-layout and communication optimisations. Rethink parts of the generative model architecture to make them more suitable for efficient inference, in collaboration with Research Scientists. Integrate low-level efficient code into a high-level MLOps framework , so that optimisations benefit every training run and deployment rather than a single experiment. Profile, benchmark and squeeze performance out of large-scale training and inference on thousands of GPUs. Model LLM execution on various GPUs with high fidelity to assess hardware usage and build serving performance estimates. What We're Looking For High technical competence for writing custom low-level kernels and pushing GPUs to their limits. High expertise in the distributed computation infrastructure of current-generation GPU clusters. Overall understanding of the field of generative AI ; knowledge of, or interest in, fine-tuning and using language models for applications. Strong software-design instincts: testing, code review, CI/CD. Self-starter, low-ego, collaborative. What We Offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page . Privacy Policy Your privacy matters to us.
